Figure layout

Source: R/zz-gen-layout.R
go_layout.Rd

Layout properties of a figure: axes, title, legend, margins, fonts and other settings that are not specific to a trace.

Usage

go_layout(
  ...,
  activeselection = NULL,
  activeshape = NULL,
  annotations = NULL,
  autosize = NULL,
  autotypenumbers = NULL,
  barcornerradius = NULL,
  bargap = NULL,
  bargroupgap = NULL,
  barmode = NULL,
  barnorm = NULL,
  boxgap = NULL,
  boxgroupgap = NULL,
  boxmode = NULL,
  calendar = NULL,
  clickanywhere = NULL,
  clickmode = NULL,
  coloraxis = NULL,
  colorscale = NULL,
  colorway = NULL,
  computed = NULL,
  datarevision = NULL,
  dragmode = NULL,
  editrevision = NULL,
  extendfunnelareacolors = NULL,
  extendiciclecolors = NULL,
  extendpiecolors = NULL,
  extendsunburstcolors = NULL,
  extendtreemapcolors = NULL,
  font = NULL,
  funnelareacolorway = NULL,
  funnelgap = NULL,
  funnelgroupgap = NULL,
  funnelmode = NULL,
  geo = NULL,
  grid = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  hiddenlabels = NULL,
  hoveranywhere = NULL,
  hoverdistance = NULL,
  hoverlabel = NULL,
  hovermode = NULL,
  hoversort = NULL,
  hoversubplots = NULL,
  iciclecolorway = NULL,
  images = NULL,
  legend = NULL,
  map = NULL,
  margin = NULL,
  meta = NULL,
  minreducedheight = NULL,
  minreducedwidth = NULL,
  modebar = NULL,
  newselection = NULL,
  newshape = NULL,
  paper_bgcolor = NULL,
  piecolorway = NULL,
  plot_bgcolor = NULL,
  polar = NULL,
  scattergap = NULL,
  scattermode = NULL,
  scene = NULL,
  selectdirection = NULL,
  selectionrevision = NULL,
  selections = NULL,
  separators = NULL,
  shapes = NULL,
  showlegend = NULL,
  sliders = NULL,
  smith = NULL,
  spikedistance = NULL,
  sunburstcolorway = NULL,
  template = NULL,
  ternary = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  transition = NULL,
  treemapcolorway = NULL,
  uirevision = NULL,
  uniformtext = NULL,
  updatemenus = NULL,
  violingap = NULL,
  violingroupgap = NULL,
  violinmode = NULL,
  waterfallgap = NULL,
  waterfallgroupgap = NULL,
  waterfallmode = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  xaxis = NULL,
  yaxis = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

Arguments

...

Not for properties, which must be named in full: an abbreviated or unknown name is an error that suggests the right one. Numbered subplots (xaxis2, scene3, ...) are given here.

activeselection

A go_activeselection() object or named list, with properties fillcolor and opacity (see go_activeselection()).

activeshape

A go_activeshape() object or named list, with properties fillcolor and opacity (see go_activeshape()).

annotations

List, each element a go_annotation() object or named list, with properties align, arrowcolor, arrowhead, arrowside, arrowsize, arrowwidth, ax, axref, ay, ayref, bgcolor, bordercolor and 31 more (see go_annotation()).

autosize

Determines whether or not a layout width or height that has been left undefined by the user is initialized on each relayout. Note that, regardless of this attribute, an undefined layout width or height is always initialized on the first call to plot. Logical.

autotypenumbers

Using "strict" a numeric string in trace data is not converted to a number. Using "convert types" a numeric string in trace data may be treated as a number during automatic axis `type` detection. This is the default value; however it could be overridden for individual axes. One of "convert types", "strict".

barcornerradius

Sets the rounding of bar corners. May be an integer number of pixels, or a percentage of bar width (as a string ending in %). Any value.

bargap

Sets the gap (in plot fraction) between bars of adjacent location coordinates. Number in the interval [0, 1].

bargroupgap

Sets the gap (in plot fraction) between bars of the same location coordinate. Number in the interval [0, 1].

barmode

Determines how bars at the same location coordinate are displayed on the graph. With "stack", the bars are stacked on top of one another With "relative", the bars are stacked on top of one another, with negative values below the axis, positive values above With "group", the bars are plotted next to one another centered around the shared location. With "overlay", the bars are plotted over one another, you might need to reduce "opacity" to see multiple bars. One of "stack", "group", "overlay", "relative".

barnorm

Sets the normalization for bar traces on the graph. With "fraction", the value of each bar is divided by the sum of all values at that location coordinate. "percent" is the same but multiplied by 100 to show percentages. One of "", "fraction", "percent".

boxgap

Sets the gap (in plot fraction) between boxes of adjacent location coordinates. Has no effect on traces that have "width" set. Number in the interval [0, 1].

boxgroupgap

Sets the gap (in plot fraction) between boxes of the same location coordinate. Has no effect on traces that have "width" set. Number in the interval [0, 1].

boxmode

Determines how boxes at the same location coordinate are displayed on the graph. If "group", the boxes are plotted next to one another centered around the shared location. If "overlay", the boxes are plotted over one another, you might need to set "opacity" to see them multiple boxes. Has no effect on traces that have "width" set. One of "group", "overlay".

calendar

Sets the default calendar system to use for interpreting and displaying dates throughout the plot. One of "chinese", "coptic", "discworld", "ethiopian", "gregorian", "hebrew", "islamic", "jalali", "julian", "mayan", "nanakshahi", "nepali", "persian", "taiwan", "thai", "ummalqura".

clickanywhere

If true, `plotly_click` events will fire for any click position within the plot area, not just over traces. When clicking where there is no trace data, the event will have an empty `points` array but will include `xvals` and `yvals` with click coordinates in data space, and `xPixel` and `yPixel` with click coordinates in pixels, relative to the top-left corner of the graph div. Logical.

clickmode

Determines the mode of single click interactions. "event" is the default value and emits the `plotly_click` event. In addition this mode emits the `plotly_selected` event in drag modes "lasso" and "select", but with no event data attached (kept for compatibility reasons). The "select" flag enables selecting single data points via click. This mode also supports persistent selections, meaning that pressing Shift while clicking, adds to / subtracts from an existing selection. "select" with `hovermode`: "x" can be confusing, consider explicitly setting `hovermode`: "closest" when using this feature. Selection events are sent accordingly as long as "event" flag is set as well. When the "event" flag is missing, `plotly_click` and `plotly_selected` events are not fired. Any combination of "event", "select" joined with "+", or one of "none".

coloraxis

A go_coloraxis() object or named list, with properties autocolorscale, cauto, cmax, cmid, cmin, colorbar, colorscale, reversescale and showscale (see go_coloraxis()).

colorscale

A go_layout_colorscale() object or named list, with properties diverging, sequential and sequentialminus (see go_layout_colorscale()).

colorway

Sets the default trace colors. Vector of colors.

computed

Placeholder for exporting automargin-impacting values namely `margin.t`, `margin.b`, `margin.l` and `margin.r` in "full-json" mode. Any value.

datarevision

If provided, a changed value tells `Plotly.react` that one or more data arrays has changed. This way you can modify arrays in-place rather than making a complete new copy for an incremental change. If NOT provided, `Plotly.react` assumes that data arrays are being treated as immutable, thus any data array with a different identity from its predecessor contains new data. Any value.

dragmode

Determines the mode of drag interactions. "select" and "lasso" apply only to scatter traces with markers or text. "orbit" and "turntable" apply only to 3D scenes. One of "zoom", "pan", "select", "lasso", "drawclosedpath", "drawopenpath", "drawline", "drawrect", "drawcircle", "orbit", "turntable", FALSE.

editrevision

Controls persistence of user-driven changes in `editable: true` configuration, other than trace names and axis titles. Defaults to `layout.uirevision`. Any value.

extendfunnelareacolors

If `true`, the funnelarea slice colors (whether given by `funnelareacolorway` or inherited from `colorway`) will be extended to three times its original length by first repeating every color 20% lighter then each color 20% darker. This is intended to reduce the likelihood of reusing the same color when you have many slices, but you can set `false` to disable. Colors provided in the trace, using `marker.colors`, are never extended. Logical.

extendiciclecolors

If `true`, the icicle slice colors (whether given by `iciclecolorway` or inherited from `colorway`) will be extended to three times its original length by first repeating every color 20% lighter then each color 20% darker. This is intended to reduce the likelihood of reusing the same color when you have many slices, but you can set `false` to disable. Colors provided in the trace, using `marker.colors`, are never extended. Logical.

extendpiecolors

If `true`, the pie slice colors (whether given by `piecolorway` or inherited from `colorway`) will be extended to three times its original length by first repeating every color 20% lighter then each color 20% darker. This is intended to reduce the likelihood of reusing the same color when you have many slices, but you can set `false` to disable. Colors provided in the trace, using `marker.colors`, are never extended. Logical.

extendsunburstcolors

If `true`, the sunburst slice colors (whether given by `sunburstcolorway` or inherited from `colorway`) will be extended to three times its original length by first repeating every color 20% lighter then each color 20% darker. This is intended to reduce the likelihood of reusing the same color when you have many slices, but you can set `false` to disable. Colors provided in the trace, using `marker.colors`, are never extended. Logical.

extendtreemapcolors

If `true`, the treemap slice colors (whether given by `treemapcolorway` or inherited from `colorway`) will be extended to three times its original length by first repeating every color 20% lighter then each color 20% darker. This is intended to reduce the likelihood of reusing the same color when you have many slices, but you can set `false` to disable. Colors provided in the trace, using `marker.colors`, are never extended. Logical.

font

Sets the global font. Note that fonts used in traces and other layout components inherit from the global font. A go_font() object or named list, with properties color, family, lineposition, shadow, size, style, textcase, variant and weight (see go_font()).

funnelareacolorway

Sets the default funnelarea slice colors. Defaults to the main `colorway` used for trace colors. If you specify a new list here it can still be extended with lighter and darker colors, see `extendfunnelareacolors`. Vector of colors.

funnelgap

Sets the gap (in plot fraction) between bars of adjacent location coordinates. Number in the interval [0, 1].

funnelgroupgap

Sets the gap (in plot fraction) between bars of the same location coordinate. Number in the interval [0, 1].

funnelmode

Determines how bars at the same location coordinate are displayed on the graph. With "stack", the bars are stacked on top of one another With "group", the bars are plotted next to one another centered around the shared location. With "overlay", the bars are plotted over one another, you might need to reduce "opacity" to see multiple bars. One of "stack", "group", "overlay".

geo

A go_geo() object or named list, with properties bgcolor, center, coastlinecolor, coastlinewidth, countrycolor, countrywidth, domain, fitbounds, framecolor, framewidth, lakecolor, landcolor and 20 more (see go_geo()).

grid

A go_grid() object or named list, with properties columns, domain, pattern, roworder, rows, subplots, xaxes, xgap, xside, yaxes, ygap and yside (see go_grid()).

height

Sets the plot's height (in px). Number in the interval [10, Inf].

hiddenlabels

hiddenlabels is the funnelarea & pie chart analog of visible:'legendonly' but it can contain many labels, and can simultaneously hide slices from several pies/funnelarea charts Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

hoveranywhere

If true, `plotly_hover` events will fire for any cursor position within the plot area, not just over traces. When the cursor is not over a trace, the event will have an empty `points` array but will include `xvals` and `yvals` with cursor coordinates in data space, and `xPixel` and `yPixel` with cursor coordinates in pixels, relative to the top-left corner of the graph div. A `plotly_unhover` event fires when the cursor leaves the plot area. Logical.

hoverdistance

Sets the default distance (in pixels) to look for data to add hover labels (-1 means no cutoff, 0 means no looking for data). This is only a real distance for hovering on point-like objects, like scatter points. For area-like objects (bars, scatter fills, etc) hovering is on inside the area and off outside, but these objects will not supersede hover on point-like objects in case of conflict. Integer in the interval [-1, Inf].

hoverlabel

A go_hoverlabel() object or named list, with properties align, bgcolor, bordercolor, font, grouptitlefont, namelength and showarrow (see go_hoverlabel()).

hovermode

Determines the mode of hover interactions. If "closest", a single hoverlabel will appear for the "closest" point within the `hoverdistance`. If "x" (or "y"), multiple hoverlabels will appear for multiple points at the "closest" x- (or y-) coordinate within the `hoverdistance`, with the caveat that no more than one hoverlabel will appear per trace. If "x unified" (or "y unified"), a single hoverlabel will appear multiple points at the closest x- (or y-) coordinate within the `hoverdistance` with the caveat that no more than one hoverlabel will appear per trace. In this mode, spikelines are enabled by default perpendicular to the specified axis. If false, hover interactions are disabled. One of "x", "y", "closest", "x unified", "y unified", FALSE.

hoversort

Determines the order of items shown in unified hover labels. If "trace", items are sorted by trace index. If "value descending", items are sorted by value from largest to smallest. If "value ascending", items are sorted by value from smallest to largest. Only applies when `hovermode` is "x unified" or "y unified". One of "trace", "value descending", "value ascending".

hoversubplots

Determines expansion of hover effects to other subplots If "single" just the axis pair of the primary point is included without overlaying subplots. If "overlaying" all subplots using the main axis and occupying the same space are included. If "axis", also include stacked subplots using the same axis when `hovermode` is set to "x", "x unified", "y" or "y unified". One of "single", "overlaying", "axis".

iciclecolorway

Sets the default icicle slice colors. Defaults to the main `colorway` used for trace colors. If you specify a new list here it can still be extended with lighter and darker colors, see `extendiciclecolors`. Vector of colors.

images

List, each element a go_layout_image() object or named list, with properties layer, name, opacity, sizex, sizey, sizing, source, templateitemname, visible, x, xanchor, xref, y, yanchor and yref (see go_layout_image()).

legend

A go_legend() object or named list, with properties bgcolor, bordercolor, borderwidth, entrywidth, entrywidthmode, font, groupclick, groupdoubleclick, grouptitlefont, indentation, itemclick, itemdoubleclick and 19 more (see go_legend()).

map

A go_map() object or named list, with properties bearing, bounds, center, domain, fitbounds, layers, pitch, style, uirevision and zoom (see go_map()).

margin

A go_margin() object or named list, with properties autoexpand, b, l, pad, r and t (see go_margin()).

meta

Assigns extra meta information that can be used in various `text` attributes. Attributes such as the graph, axis and colorbar `title.text`, annotation `text` `trace.name` in legend items, `rangeselector`, `updatemenus` and `sliders` `label` text all support `meta`. One can access `meta` fields using template strings: `%{meta[i]}` where `i` is the index of the `meta` item in question. `meta` can also be an object for example `{key: value}` which can be accessed %{meta[key]}. Any value.

minreducedheight

Minimum height of the plot with margin.automargin applied (in px) Number in the interval [2, Inf].

minreducedwidth

Minimum width of the plot with margin.automargin applied (in px) Number in the interval [2, Inf].

modebar

A go_modebar() object or named list, with properties activecolor, add, bgcolor, color, orientation, remove and uirevision (see go_modebar()).

newselection

A go_newselection() object or named list, with properties line and mode (see go_newselection()).

newshape

A go_newshape() object or named list, with properties drawdirection, fillcolor, fillrule, label, layer, legend, legendgroup, legendgrouptitle, legendrank, legendwidth, line, name, opacity, showlegend and visible (see go_newshape()).

paper_bgcolor

Sets the background color of the paper where the graph is drawn. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

piecolorway

Sets the default pie slice colors. Defaults to the main `colorway` used for trace colors. If you specify a new list here it can still be extended with lighter and darker colors, see `extendpiecolors`. Vector of colors.

plot_bgcolor

Sets the background color of the plotting area in-between x and y axes. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

polar

A go_polar() object or named list, with properties angularaxis, bargap, barmode, bgcolor, domain, gridshape, hole, radialaxis, sector and uirevision (see go_polar()).

scattergap

Sets the gap (in plot fraction) between scatter points of adjacent location coordinates. Defaults to `bargap`. Number in the interval [0, 1].

scattermode

Determines how scatter points at the same location coordinate are displayed on the graph. With "group", the scatter points are plotted next to one another centered around the shared location. With "overlay", the scatter points are plotted over one another, you might need to reduce "opacity" to see multiple scatter points. One of "group", "overlay".

scene

A go_scene() object or named list, with properties annotations, aspectmode, aspectratio, bgcolor, camera, domain, dragmode, hovermode, uirevision, xaxis, yaxis and zaxis (see go_scene()).

selectdirection

When `dragmode` is set to "select", this limits the selection of the drag to horizontal, vertical or diagonal. "h" only allows horizontal selection, "v" only vertical, "d" only diagonal and "any" sets no limit. One of "h", "v", "d", "any".

selectionrevision

Controls persistence of user-driven changes in selected points from all traces. Any value.

selections

List, each element a go_selection() object or named list, with properties line, name, opacity, path, templateitemname, type, x0, x1, xref, y0, y1 and yref (see go_selection()).

separators

Sets the decimal and thousand separators. For example, ". " puts a '.' before decimals and a space between thousands. In English locales, dflt is ".," but other locales may alter this default. String.

shapes

List, each element a go_shape() object or named list, with properties editable, fillcolor, fillrule, label, layer, legend, legendgroup, legendgrouptitle, legendrank, legendwidth, line, name and 20 more (see go_shape()).

showlegend

Determines whether or not a legend is drawn. Default is `true` if there is a trace to show and any of these: a) Two or more traces would by default be shown in the legend. b) One pie trace is shown in the legend. c) One trace is explicitly given with `showlegend: true`. Logical.

sliders

List, each element a go_slider() object or named list, with properties active, activebgcolor, bgcolor, bordercolor, borderwidth, currentvalue, font, len, lenmode, minorticklen, name, pad and 11 more (see go_slider()).

smith

A go_smith() object or named list, with properties bgcolor, domain, imaginaryaxis and realaxis (see go_smith()).

spikedistance

Sets the default distance (in pixels) to look for data to draw spikelines to (-1 means no cutoff, 0 means no looking for data). As with hoverdistance, distance does not apply to area-like objects. In addition, some objects can be hovered on but will not generate spikelines, such as scatter fills. Integer in the interval [-1, Inf].

sunburstcolorway

Sets the default sunburst slice colors. Defaults to the main `colorway` used for trace colors. If you specify a new list here it can still be extended with lighter and darker colors, see `extendsunburstcolors`. Vector of colors.

template

Default attributes to be applied to the plot. Templates can be created from existing plots using `Plotly.makeTemplate`, or created manually. They should be objects with format: `{layout: layoutTemplate, data: {[type]: [traceTemplate, ...]}, ...}` `layoutTemplate` and `traceTemplate` are objects matching the attribute structure of `layout` and a data trace. Trace templates are applied cyclically to traces of each type. Container arrays (eg `annotations`) have special handling: An object ending in `defaults` (eg `annotationdefaults`) is applied to each array item. But if an item has a `templateitemname` key we look in the template array for an item with matching `name` and apply that instead. If no matching `name` is found we mark the item invisible. Any named template item not referenced is appended to the end of the array, so you can use this for a watermark annotation or a logo image, for example. To omit one of these items on the plot, make an item with matching `templateitemname` and `visible: false`. Any value.

ternary

A go_ternary() object or named list, with properties aaxis, baxis, bgcolor, caxis, domain, sum and uirevision (see go_ternary()).

title

String (the title text), or a go_layout_title() object or named list, with properties automargin, font, pad, subtitle, text, x, xanchor, xref, y, yanchor and yref (see go_layout_title()).

transition

Sets transition options used during Plotly.react updates. A go_layout_transition() object or named list, with properties duration, easing and ordering (see go_layout_transition()).

treemapcolorway

Sets the default treemap slice colors. Defaults to the main `colorway` used for trace colors. If you specify a new list here it can still be extended with lighter and darker colors, see `extendtreemapcolors`. Vector of colors.

uirevision

Used to allow user interactions with the plot to persist after `Plotly.react` calls that are unaware of these interactions. If `uirevision` is omitted, or if it is given and it changed from the previous `Plotly.react` call, the exact new figure is used. If `uirevision` is truthy and did NOT change, any attribute that has been affected by user interactions and did not receive a different value in the new figure will keep the interaction value. `layout.uirevision` attribute serves as the default for `uirevision` attributes in various sub-containers. For finer control you can set these sub-attributes directly. For example, if your app separately controls the data on the x and y axes you might set `xaxis.uirevision="time"` and `yaxis.uirevision="cost"`. Then if only the y data is changed, you can update `yaxis.uirevision="quantity"` and the y axis range will reset but the x axis range will retain any user-driven zoom. Any value.

uniformtext

A go_uniformtext() object or named list, with properties minsize and mode (see go_uniformtext()).

updatemenus

List, each element a go_updatemenu() object or named list, with properties active, bgcolor, bordercolor, borderwidth, buttons, direction, font, name, pad, showactive, templateitemname, type and 5 more (see go_updatemenu()).

violingap

Sets the gap (in plot fraction) between violins of adjacent location coordinates. Has no effect on traces that have "width" set. Number in the interval [0, 1].

violingroupgap

Sets the gap (in plot fraction) between violins of the same location coordinate. Has no effect on traces that have "width" set. Number in the interval [0, 1].

violinmode

Determines how violins at the same location coordinate are displayed on the graph. If "group", the violins are plotted next to one another centered around the shared location. If "overlay", the violins are plotted over one another, you might need to set "opacity" to see them multiple violins. Has no effect on traces that have "width" set. One of "group", "overlay".

waterfallgap

Sets the gap (in plot fraction) between bars of adjacent location coordinates. Number in the interval [0, 1].

waterfallgroupgap

Sets the gap (in plot fraction) between bars of the same location coordinate. Number in the interval [0, 1].

waterfallmode

Determines how bars at the same location coordinate are displayed on the graph. With "group", the bars are plotted next to one another centered around the shared location. With "overlay", the bars are plotted over one another, you might need to reduce "opacity" to see multiple bars. One of "group", "overlay".

width

Sets the plot's width (in px). Number in the interval [10, Inf].

xaxis

A go_xaxis() object or named list, with properties anchor, automargin, autorange, autorangeoptions, autotickangles, autotypenumbers, calendar, categoryarray, categoryorder, color, constrain, constraintoward and 80 more (see go_xaxis()).

yaxis

A go_yaxis() object or named list, with properties anchor, automargin, autorange, autorangeoptions, autoshift, autotickangles, autotypenumbers, calendar, categoryarray, categoryorder, color, constrain and 80 more (see go_yaxis()).

skip_invalid

If TRUE, silently drop invalid properties instead of raising an error.

Value

go_*() functions return a graph object; add_*() functions return the modified figure.

Details

go_layout() creates a validated graph object (a named list).

Nested objects are given as named lists or with their constructors, which are linked from the arguments below. Every property is checked against the plotly.js schema when the object is created or modified (see plotly_obj-modify). One-sided formulas (~col) are evaluated in the data, and then checked, when the trace is added with add_<trace>() or add_trace().

See also

go_figure(), update_layout()

Examples

go_layout(title = "My plot", xaxis = go_xaxis(title = "x", range = c(0, 10)))
#> <go_layout>
#> {
#>   "title": {
#>     "text": "My plot"
#>   },
#>   "xaxis": {
#>     "range": [
#>       0,
#>       10
#>     ],
#>     "title": {
#>       "text": "x"
#>     }
#>   }
#> }
#>
